styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Civil rights sites, MLK park and old Atlanta.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Southern classics, BBQ and a strong global food scene.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Piedmont Park, the BeltLine and the Botanical Garden.

stays.why: Walk to the Georgia Aquarium, World of Coca-Cola and the National Center for Civil and Human Rights. Streetcar and MARTA nearby.
Central and lively: Piedmont Park, the High Museum and many restaurants. Good MARTA rail access.
Quieter, upscale shopping and dining. Further from downtown sights but easy by car or ride app.
Leafy neighborhood feel with local bars and cafés. Close to the BeltLine and Piedmont Park.

food: Try Southern staples: fried chicken, shrimp and grits, collard greens and peach desserts.
Look for BBQ spots for pulled pork, ribs and brisket; portions are big and prices vary.
The BeltLine and Ponce City Market area has many casual and sit-down options in one place.
Cheap eats: diners, taquerias and food halls around Midtown and Downtown, often $10–20 a meal.
Book ahead for popular weekend brunch; lines get long. Check hours on the day for smaller spots.
more_time: Swap a city afternoon for the Atlanta Botanical Garden or a walk on the BeltLine if the weather is good.
History fans can add a half-day at the Martin Luther King Jr. National Historical Park.
With kids, the Georgia Aquarium can easily fill a morning; book timed tickets ahead.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the civil rights sights, the aquarium and a good food day; add a night for nature and neighborhoods.

month_notes: January: cold, highs near 11°C and lows near 2°C. Pack a warm layer.
February: still cool, highs around 15°C. Rain on about 12 days.
March: mild and warming, highs near 18°C. Good for walking.
April: pleasant, highs around 22°C. One of the best months to visit.
May: warm, highs near 26°C. Expect some rain days.
June: hot, highs around 30°C. Plan indoor breaks midday.
July: hottest and wettest, highs near 31°C and about 17 rain days.
August: hot and humid, highs near 30°C. Storms are common.
September: still warm, highs near 28°C, with fewer rain days.
October: comfortable, highs around 23°C. Great for parks and the BeltLine.
November: cooler, highs near 17°C. Light rain on about 8 days.
December: chilly, highs around 13°C and lows near 5°C. Bring a coat.

climate_guide.summary: Humid subtropical: mild springs and falls, hot humid summers with storms, and short cool winters.

items.title: Best time: April to May and September to October
items.text: Mild highs around 22–28°C and fewer rain days. Ideal for walking and parks.

items.title: Summer is hot and humid (June to August)
items.text: Highs near 30–31°C with about 14–17 rain days a month. Do outdoor sights in the morning.

items.title: Afternoon storms
items.text: July and August bring the most rain days. Keep a plan B indoors.

items.title: Winter is cool, not freezing
items.text: January highs near 11°C and lows near 2°C. A warm jacket is enough.

items.title: Rain spread through the year
items.text: Most months see 8–17 rain days. A small umbrella helps any trip.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light layers in spring and fall, breathable clothes and sunscreen for summer, a warm coat for winter.

transit.best: MARTA rail and ride apps for most trips; walk downtown and Midtown.

modes.text: MARTA rail has four lines (Red, Gold, Blue, Green). $2.50 per ride, $9 for a 1-day pass. Breeze Card costs $2 and is reloadable; tap on entry and exit.
Buses cover 100+ routes, but weekend waits can reach an hour.
Uber and Lyft work widely. Taxis are available but less common.
Driving is fastest off-peak. Rush hour is long and parking downtown is scarce.
Downtown is walkable and the Atlanta Streetcar links key sights. Bikes are an option.
The Atlanta Streetcar links key downtown sights.
